meta.label: Client edition 016
meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 1.12% to 25,800.60 as Nifty Bank gained 2.49%; foreign investors bought ₹10,308 crore (provisional); the S&P 500 fell 3.70% overnight.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Mon 23 Nov: NIFTY 50 rises 1.12% to 25,800.60; banks gain 2.49%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 1.12% to 25,800.60 and the Sensex 1.08% to 83,919.71 on Friday, both nine-month highs; Nifty Bank rose 2.49% to 64,635.20 (HDFC Sky, Business Standard). Over the week the NIFTY 50 gained 2.61% (Business Standard).
The NIFTY Midcap 100 rose 0.66% and the Smallcap 100 slipped 0.13%; Nifty Media fell 1.68%, the weakest sector (Business Standard).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹10,308 crore and domestic institutions sold a net ₹4,860 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo). The rupee closed near 92.67 per dollar, a seven-month high (Reuters, HDFC Sky).
After India closed, the S&P 500 fell 3.70% and the Nasdaq 5.28% on Friday as AI-linked shares were sold; the S&P 500 entered correction territory (investingLive, Investrade).
IBJA's Friday afternoon rate put gold at ₹1,23,893 per 10 g, down 4.35% from Thursday afternoon; spot gold fell 2.38% to about $3,538 an ounce (IBJA, Kitco).

outlook.headline: Foreign buying, the rupee, crude and Friday's fall in US shares frame a short week

drivers.title: Foreign buying
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹10,308 crore on Friday and ₹1,11,949 crore from 1 to 20 November (provisional, Kotak Neo); Kotak Neo said it was a fourth straight week of foreign buying. Flows reach large financials, the largest weight in the NIFTY 50, and the rupee.

drivers.title: Crude and the rupee
drivers.text: Reuters reported Brent heading for a third weekly fall as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels, and the rupee closed near 92.67 per dollar, a seven-month high (Reuters). Oil reaches India through the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Inflation and the RBI
drivers.text: October retail inflation was 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit; Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments said markets may start to price in a possible rate rise (Kotak Neo). Policy rates reach bank lending rates and bond yields.

global_cues.title: US shares
global_cues.text: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% and the Nasdaq 5.28% on Friday, after India had closed (investingLive); today is the first Indian session after that fall. US moves reach India through foreign flows and US-exposed sectors such as IT.

global_cues.title: US yields and the Fed
global_cues.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.91% (Newsquawk), and Fed Governor Lisa Cook said policy was not restrictive enough (Newsquawk). US rates reach India through the dollar, the rupee and emerging-market flows.

events.title: November derivatives expiry
events.text: NSE's November 2026 derivatives contracts expire today (JM Financial).

events.title: Market holiday
events.text: NSE and BSE are closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti (Angel One).

events.title: India's GDP for July to September
events.text: Forecasts reported by Business Today include 7.4% from Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis, about 7.8% from SBI Ecowrap and 7.2% from the RBI.

events.title: Fed policy meeting
events.text: The Federal Reserve meets on 8 and 9 Dec; USAGOLD, citing CME FedWatch, put the chance of a quarter-point rise at about 99%.

global.headline: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% and entered correction territory as AI-linked shares were sold
global.note: Closes are for Friday 20 Nov. Other Asian closes are not shown because only one published source gave the level.

us.title: The session
us.text: US shares fell for a seventh straight session as investors sold AI-linked shares, from chipmakers to data-centre suppliers; the S&P 500 entered correction territory and the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gain (investingLive, Investrade).

us.title: Chip shares
us.text: Nvidia fell 13.8% after Reuters reported that the SEC was examining its accounting, and Broadcom fell about 12% on a report that Google had cut planned 2027 chip shipments (Newsquawk).

us.title: Bonds and volatility
us.text: Treasuries rose and the 10-year yield fell back below 5%; the VIX volatility index closed above 37 (Newsquawk, Investrade).

extras.label: US 10-year yield
extras.detail: Down about 14 basis points (Newsquawk); investingLive quoted about 4.94%

events.title: Markets price a December Fed rise
events.text: Fed Governor Lisa Cook said policy was not restrictive enough, and markets price a quarter-point rise in December (Newsquawk; CME FedWatch via Investrade). The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: Reports of a possible strike on Iran
events.text: Newsquawk linked Friday's rise in crude to a CBS report that the US and Israel were weighing a new attack on Iran. The channel to India: the import bill, fuel inflation and the rupee.

events.title: Asia's worst week since 2020
events.text: Reuters said Asian shares were heading for their worst week since 2020 as AI-linked shares fell; the Nikkei and the Kospi each fell more than 5% on Friday (Goodreturns). The channel to India: foreign flows across emerging markets.

metals.headline: IBJA's Friday afternoon rate put gold at ₹1,23,893 per 10 g, down 4.35% from Thursday; spot gold fell 2.38%

commentary.text: Kitco said gold and silver fell along with shares as the S&P 500 entered correction territory, and read the move as selling of metals rather than buying for safety; it said silver fell more on worries about industrial demand.
USAGOLD, citing CME FedWatch, put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December at about 99%; higher rates raise the cost of holding gold, which pays no interest.
USAGOLD, citing CNBC, said gold lost about 8% over the week, its largest weekly fall since the week ended 20 March.

stories.headline: Shriram Finance is to replace Trent in the Sensex
stories.what: BSE Index Services said on 20 Nov that Shriram Finance will replace Trent in the Sensex from 21 Dec 2026, and Divi's Laboratories will replace Wipro in the Sensex 50 (Kotak Neo).
stories.why: Index funds and ETFs that track these indices rebalance on the effective date, which brings buying and selling in the shares added and removed.

stories.headline: SEBI proposes easing disclosure rules for some foreign investors
stories.what: SEBI proposed removing the additional disclosure framework for foreign portfolio investors with large holdings in one group or in Indian equity, and invited comments until 11 Dec 2026 (Kotak Neo).
stories.why: The rules shape how easily foreign investors can be onboarded and invest in Indian shares.

stories.headline: IndusInd Bank ends its former CEO's employment after an inquiry
stories.what: IndusInd Bank's board terminated former CEO Sumant Kathpalia's employment on 20 Nov and invoked malus and clawback provisions back to March 2020 (Kotak Neo). HDFC Sky reported that the bank's shares rose 8.6% that day.
stories.why: It is a governance development at a large private bank, in a sector with a heavy index weight.

learn.title: What a credit rating such as AA+ tells you
paragraphs: A credit rating, such as AAA, AA+ or AA−, is a symbol that rating agencies such as CRISIL and CARE give a borrower's bonds. It sums up the borrower's creditworthiness: its ability to repay interest and principal (DSP Mutual Fund).

Higher ratings indicate relatively higher safety, and such borrowers usually pay lower interest. Even a high rating does not rule out a default, and a rating can be upgraded or downgraded as the borrower's position changes (DSP Mutual Fund).

SEBI's categories use ratings: a corporate bond fund must invest at least 80% of its assets in corporate bonds rated AA+ and above (AMFI). A fund's factsheet shows how its holdings are spread across rating levels.
